title: Broad Street Station at its height, 1943 (the set's views)
about: The set's close views of the station take the station's history (history/broad-street-station.json, which the cutaway, already sold, is drawn from) with the rules the set's other views follow: parking aisles and drives dated with surface parking, service roads only beside a building of the year, laid-out ground and service roads dated by their parcel, verges and bridge approaches dated with their roads.

rules.note: The drive before the station's front, taken to be the station's own approach of 1919 rather than a later driveway (approximate: no plan of the drive is cited).
The Diamond opened in April 1985 on the site of Parker Field (built in 1934 as part of the fair grounds, a ballpark from 1954).
The R&P bridge, rebuilt on concrete piers in 1902 and removed in 1970; its piers stand today. Its approaches are not mapped, so its ends are drawn where OSM's way ends (approximate).
Disused and abandoned track mapped today: no source here says when each piece last carried trains, so none is drawn in the past (it would float as pieces of live track). Undated: each needs a source.
The roundabout at the Seventh Street ramps of the I-64/I-95 interchange, part of the interstate's works: drawn today only (approximate, not sourced).
Ramps and turning roads of the interchanges, dated with the turnpike: approximate, not sourced.
Settling basins, stormwater basins and pools: none is dated by a source here (the treatment plant's basins and the basins of the interstate's drainage among them), so they are drawn today only.
Basins: drawn today only, as above.
Treatment works and tanks: not dated here, drawn today only.
Paths, footbridges among them (the Potterfield bridge on the old dam at Brown's Island, of 2016), are not dated: drawn in today's view only.
Parking aisles, driveways and drive-throughs, dated with surface parking, as in the downtown series: approximate, not sourced.

dates.name: Sauer Center parking deck
dates.note: A five-level deck planned in May 2019 on the surface lot behind 2220 W. Broad Street; dated 2020 (approximate: built after the plan). The parcel's recorded year (1910) is an older building's.

dates.name: Cookie Factory tower
dates.note: The factory's first building, a six-storey tower completed in 1927; the company added to it through the 1940s and 1950s.

dates.name: Virginia Museum of Fine Arts
dates.note: Today's outline takes in the wings of 1954, 1970, 1976, 1984 and 2010 around the 1936 building facing the Boulevard. The 1936 building alone is not mapped, so the museum is not drawn before the outline was complete (approximate: it stood from 1936).

features.name: Broad Street Station dome
features.note: The dome: a cornice ring, the stepped haunches and the low outer dome, in its original tile in 1943; inside, the hall's ceiling, a shallower vault. Profiles from sections A-A, B-B and C-C; the crown is 100 ft above the floor, as published. In the set's views the dome is in the tile it kept until 1955, when copper replaced it.
